summary: Adds an immutable Email value object with normalization, validation and value equality, plus unit tests. The change is clean and low risk; the only note is that the raw address is echoed in the error message.

findings.summary: Raw email address is included in the error message
findings.rationale: The DomainError message interpolates raw, the address the caller supplied, so every rejected address is carried in the exception text. Errors of this kind are normally logged and are often returned to the client, which puts personal data into log storage that outlives the request and is read by people with no reason to see it. It is a small leak on one line, and the kind that spreads once the pattern is copied into the next value object.
findings.suggestion: Throw a constant message such as 'Invalid email address' and attach the field name rather than the value. If a concrete value genuinely helps debugging, mask it - j***@example.com - so the log says what shape of input failed without recording who it belonged to.

dropped.summary: Email pattern rejects addresses with uppercase letters
dropped.note: The character classes accept any non-space, non-@ character, and create() lowercases the input before testing.
